Mar Zutra's premise: the altar rose one amah and indented one -- the yesod; rose five and indented one -- the sovev; rose three -- the place of the horns
(within the hypothesis) then how could [eleven-amah willows] lean over the altar?
R' Abbahu: what is the verse? 'isru chag ba'avotim until the horns of the altar' (Tehillim 118:27)
R' Elazar: whoever takes a lulav in its binding and a myrtle in its avot -- the verse reckons it to him as though he built an altar and offered a sacrifice on it
R' Elazar's source: 'isru chag ba'avotim until the horns of the altar' (Tehillim 118:27) [Steinsaltz: isru = bind the lulav, avotim = the myrtle]
whoever makes an isur to the festival with eating and drinking -- the verse reckons it to him as though he built an altar and offered a sacrifice on it
its source: 'isru chag ba'avotim until the horns of the altar' (Tehillim 118:27) [Steinsaltz: isru = add to the festival, avotim = fattened animals]
RSbY: in all the mitzvot one fulfils one's obligation only [with the object held] in the manner of its growth
RSbY's source: 'acacia wood, standing' (Shemot 26:15)
the baraita: 'acacia wood, standing' -- they stand in the manner of their growth
the baraita, alternatively: 'standing' -- they hold up their plating

Rava: the row before the Holy One, Blessed be He, is eighteen thousand, as it says 'round about, eighteen thousand' (Yechezkel 48:35)
the stam's distinction: the one [statement concerns] those who look through the bright speculum, the other those who do not
Abaye: the world has no fewer than thirty-six righteous who greet the Shekhina every day, as it says 'happy are all who wait for Him (lo)' (Yeshayahu 30:18) -- lo in gematria is thirty-six
the stam's second distinction: the one [statement concerns] those who enter with permission, the other those who enter without permission
